Q: Add value from a list to emacs radio-button-choice widget A:

You're attempting to pass the function widget-create a single argument which is the list ((item "creds") (item "token")) when you need to be passing it two independent arguments (item "creds") and (item "token")

You're actually passing it ((item x) (item x)) though, so you have two problems.

You need to use apply to convert a list of arguments into a sequence of individual arguments for a function call:

  (apply #'widget-create
         'radio-button-choice
         :value "One"
         :notify (lambda (widget &rest ignore)
                   (message "You selected %s"
                            (widget-value widget)))
         (mapcar (lambda (x) (list 'item x)) cred-types))

As the other answer mentions, you could alternatively use \(item ,x)instead of(list 'item x)` but that alone doesn't solve the problem of not having individual arguments.

As a tangent to that, though... if, instead of calling a function, you were instead generating code with a lisp macro, then you would most likely already be working with a backquoted form, and you could splice the list elements into the form using ,@(mapcar ...). (That's not useful to you here, though.)

Q: Jupyter with VSCode: "execution_count": null / NameError: name 'null' is not defined A:

Sometimes the debugger that comes with VS Code is incompatible with the version in your local environment. To fix this, execute the following in the terminal:

conda activate MY_ENV_NAME
pip install --upgrade debugpy ipykernel

After upgrading, restart the notebook. This ensures your local environment can correctly handle debug signals from VS Code.

Q: QSIG - Blender - SHP - GLB A:

Roads: visible in Blender, but empty .glb

✅ What’s happening

Roads are LINESTRING geometries

Blender + glTF cannot export pure curves / lines

BlenderGIS imports roads as curves, not meshes

glTF exporter only exports meshes

→ Result: empty .glb

✅ Fix (REQUIRED)

You must convert roads to meshes before export.

In Blender:

Select the Roads object

Object Mode → Object → Convert → Mesh

Go to Edit Mode

Select all (A)

Mesh → Clean Up → Fill Faces (if needed)

Add thickness (optional but recommended):

Modifier → Solidify

Now export to .glb

✔ Roads will appear correctly in glTF viewers and Angular

2️⃣ Buildings: only a few appear in Blender

❌ Root causes (common)

One or more of these are true:

Invalid geometries in QGIS

Buildings are MULTIPOLYGON

Buildings have no height / Z value

Some buildings are self-intersecting

BlenderGIS silently skips broken features

✅ Fix in QGIS (VERY IMPORTANT)

Step 1: Fix geometries

Vector → Geometry Tools → Fix Geometries

Export the fixed layer as SHP.

Step 2: Ensure buildings are polygons (not multipolygon)

Vector → Geometry Tools → Multipart to Singleparts

Step 3: Add height (critical for Blender)

If your buildings are flat:

Open Field Calculator

Create new field: height

Type: Decimal

Value (example):

coalesce("height", 10)

(or any default value)

Step 4: Re-export SHP

CRS: EPSG:3857 or EPSG:4326

Encoding: UTF-8

3️⃣ Boundary works fine (why?)

Because:

Boundary = simple polygon

Already a mesh

No topology issues

No curves involved

That’s why it exports cleanly to .glb.

4️⃣ BlenderGIS import settings (important)

When importing SHP in BlenderGIS:

✅ Use CRS

✅ Merge by layer

❌ Disable “Import as curves” (for roads if option exists)

Set scale correctly

5️⃣ Correct Web-Ready Workflow (RECOMMENDED)

✔ QGIS

.pbf

↓

Fix Geometries

↓

Singleparts

↓

Add height

↓

Export SHP

✔ Blender

Import via BlenderGIS

↓

Convert curves → mesh (roads)

↓

Extrude buildings

↓

Apply transforms (Ctrl+A → All)

↓

Export GLB (Apply modifiers ON)

✔ Angular / Three.js

const loader = new GLTFLoader();

loader.load('map.glb', (gltf) => {

scene.add(gltf.scene);

});

6️⃣ Why glTF Viewer shows empty file

Because:

glTF ignores curves

Roads stayed curves

Resulting .glb technically contains data, but no renderable mesh

Q: failed to load listeners: can't create unix socket /var/run/docker.sock: device or resource busy gitlab-runner A:

gitlab-runner tries to create the sock file and found out it is already there stop docker remove the docker.sock file: rm -f /var/run/docker.sock and try again

Q: How to refresh token after the access_token has expired A:

It seems like there are a couple of issues related to the package

However, refresh_token has different lifetime than the access_token you can configure it in config/jwt.php.

You just have to make sure that your refresh_token is alive as well otherwise if both expires, then user has to request another token.

Another trick to do is to set this key to null, then refresh_token will have unlimited lifetime

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Refresh time to live
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | Specify the length of time (in minutes) that the token can be refreshed
    | within. I.E. The user can refresh their token within a 2 week window of
    | the original token being created until they must re-authenticate.
    | Defaults to 2 weeks.
    |
    | You can also set this to null, to yield an infinite refresh time.
    | Some may want this instead of never expiring tokens for e.g. a mobile app.
    | This is not particularly recommended, so make sure you have appropriate
    | systems in place to revoke the token if necessary.
    |
    */

    'refresh_ttl' => env('JWT_REFRESH_TTL', 20160),
